Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our agreement on the commercial terms, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature runbook: staged rollout windows, canary validation steps, migration weekend sequencing, and the suggested training cohorts. Key asks for today: please confirm 1) the preferred canary week (we've proposed Dec 13-17), and 2) whether you want the training split across two cohorts or a single full-day session.

Highlights in the attached MAP (Ardor_MAP_v1.pdf):
- Canary validation: 3% production traffic window, synthetic regression tests + customer acceptance prompts
- Migration: dry-run on pre-prod two days prior, cutover on migration weekend (target: Jan 8-9)
- Training: admin + ops cohort (2 hours) and developer workshop (3 hours)
- Evaluation gates: latency P95 threshold, token-cost delta threshold, and user acceptance recall tests

I attached a canary_checklist.xlsx to make the cutover tasks explicit.

Next steps (my recommended sequence):
1) Ardor confirms canary week and training cadence by EOD Wed (Dec 2)
2) Redwood internal owners fill out the runbook assignments (we'll do that today)
3) Signatures / DocuSign to be sent once responsibilities are agreed

I've cc'd Marissa (on exec-level acceptance criteria) and Jonas (technical lead on the migration plan).

Best,
Sergio Alvarez

Sergio —

Thanks for the MAP and checklist. We reviewed the high level with our platform and security teams this morning. A few clarifying items:

- Canary week: Dec 13-17 works for us. We prefer the canary window to run Tue-Thu (13-15) with Wed the primary validation day.
- Training: split into two cohorts (Ops admins + Devs) — Ops cohort on Dec 20 (2 hours), Devs on Dec 22 (3 hours). Can you confirm availability for those dates?
- Audit / retention: security asked whether Redwood can provide 90-day token-level logs for the evaluation window (we need them for the acceptance test). Is that covered in the MAP?
- Migration weekend: Jan 8-9 is acceptable, but we need a dry-run on Jan 5 (small production-like exercise) instead of two days prior.

Tom will help coordinate the Ops attendees and will share a preliminary list of integrations that must be gated during the canary.

Elena —

Appreciate the quick read. Short answers inline below and a slightly expanded canary acceptance checklist in the Drive link (see related links).

- Canary window: Tue 12/13 -> Thu 12/15 (primary validation Wed 12/14) — confirmed.
- Training: two cohorts confirmed. Ops: Mon 12/20 10:00-12:00 PT. Devs: Wed 12/22 09:00-12:00 PT. I'll share invites once Jonas confirms facilitator names. Attached: training_roster_v1.csv (basic attendee roster template).
- Audit / retention: Redwood can surface token-level request/response logs for a 90-day window scoped to the evaluation traffic. For production we can enable a 30/90 retention toggle; enabling 90 days will require minimal ops config and a brief security review (we'll assign this as a dependency in the MAP).
- Dry-run: Jan 5 dry-run accepted (we'll treat it as a simulated cutover to minimize blast radius).

Canary acceptance criteria (high level):
- Functional: no user-facing regression on the top 20 customer prompts (automated test pass >= 98%)
- Performance: P95 latency within 1.5x of baseline and no throughput degradation for burst profiles
- Cost: token cost delta <= 12% vs baseline for the pilot traffic profile
- Stability: no more than two transient 5+ minute node restarts during 72h window
- Security/Audit: logs available for review within 1 hour and access controls validated

Rollback triggers: any failed automated regression or P95 > 2x baseline on validation day triggers immediate rollback and postmortem.

I've added the above acceptance items into Ardor_MAP_v1.pdf and canary_checklist.xlsx (versioned).

Marissa Cole
VP, Global Customer Success
Redwood Inference
